rfi.description: Police and demonstrators clashed in towns and cities across France on Saturday as tens of thousands of people took to the streets to protest against rising costs and the poor state of the country's schools.

rfi.title: France's new sexual violence bill 'fails to tackle root causes', campaigners warn
rfi.description: A sweeping package of reforms, passed unanimously by the lower house of parliament this week, aims to overhaul how France investigates and prosecutes sexual violence. Yet campaigners say the legislation does not do enough to prevent abuse, while protection for some of the most vulnerable victims is lacking.

rfi.title: AI midwife seeks to fill gaps in Zimbabwe's maternal health care
rfi.description: With public health services stretched thin, women in Zimbabwe sometimes struggle to access reliable information about pregnancy and childbirth. A locally developed app aims to answer their questions and direct them to appropriate care, in an example of the potential of artificial intelligence to ease pressure on overloaded health systems.

rfi.title: Pacific nations await climate billions, as fossil fuel divide looms over Cop31
rfi.description: Ahead of next month’s United Nations Cop31 climate summit, as a strengthening El Niño drives Pacific sea temperatures towards record levels, more than $5 billion promised to the region remains unpaid. Cop31 co-hosts Turkey and Australia are pushing to speed up the switch to electric transport, heating and industry, but participating countries are divided over how to wind down the use of coal, oil and gas.

rfi.title: Shipping attacks threaten Turkey's resolve to keep warships out of Black Sea
rfi.description: A wave of deadly attacks on cargo ships in the waters of NATO members Bulgaria and Romania has jolted the alliance into calling an emergency meeting on Black Sea security. Yet any move to send NATO ships hinges on Turkey reversing its steadfast refusal to allow warships into the Black Sea.

rfi.title: Zelensky says US move to waive sanctions 'rewards' Russia's Putin
rfi.description: Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky on Saturday hit out at the decision of the US President Donald Trump to block sanctions on Russia claiming the move rewarded the country's leader Vladimir Putin.

rfi.title: Madagascar marks one year since uprising as Russia’s influence grows
rfi.description: Madagascar marks one year on Saturday since military leader Michael Randrianirina took power following weeks of youth-led protests that brought down elected president Andry Rajoelina. Over the past year, Russian influence has grown through closer military ties and weapons deliveries, while researchers have identified Moscow’s interest in a strategic Indian Ocean port. Many of the political reforms demanded by protesters, however, remain unfinished.

rfi.title: Mayors urge France to recognise 1961 Paris massacre of Algerians as state crime
rfi.description: On the eve of the 65th anniversary of the massacre of Algerian protesters in Paris, French mayors are calling for the events of 17 October, 1961 to be officially recognised as a state crime.

rfi.title: School students called to join Yellow Vests and unions for mass French protest
rfi.description: Following an unsuccessful meeting with France's education minister on Thursday, protesting high school pupils across the country say they will not let up the pressure on the government. The Yellow Vests movement has called on the students to join them at a nationwide demonstration on Saturday over working conditions and the cost of living.

rfi.title: France and Germany strike deal to boost Europe's struggling car industry
rfi.description: France and Germany have agreed a deal to safeguard Europe's automobile industry and stave off fierce competition from Chinese electric car companies. The agreement also opens the door for the United Kingdom to be treated as a trusted partner under "Made in EU" rules.

rfi.title: Nineteen injured as minibus crashes into Channel Tunnel shuttle train
rfi.description: A minibus carrying truck drivers crashed into a freight train at the loading platform of the Eurotunnel injuring 19 people, French authorities said.

rfi.title: Somalia sets date for May presidential election amid ongoing Islamist insurgency
rfi.description: Somalia's election commission has announced it will hold parliamentary and presidential polls in April and May next year, but critics say the decision will lead to more conflict in a deeply fragmented country facing a long-running Islamist insurgency.

rfi.title: Infantino offers apology but 'no answers' at Fifa meeting over World Cup plan
rfi.description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino gave "no satisfactory answers" when grilled Thursday during a meeting to discuss his attempts to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, senior members of football's global governing body said, but he did offer an apology for the failed project.

rfi.title: Challenge to HIV restrictions in French armed forces goes before top court
rfi.description: Several organisations have brought a case before France’s highest court to challenge the continued exclusion of people living with HIV from certain posts in the armed forces, gendarmerie and fire services.

rfi.title: Trial of French IS returnee highlights a growing focus on the women who came back
rfi.description: Courts are increasingly turning their attention to the women who joined the Islamic State armed group in Syria and Iraq, and then returned to France. rfi.title: Belgian police raid Tshisekedi family properties in DRC mining investigation

rfi.title: Ukraine’s Starlink disruptions expose European reliance on US tech
rfi.description: Ukraine has reported disruptions to drones relying on Elon Musk's Starlink satellite internet network, as well as the United States-operated early warning system supposed to alert it to Russian missile attacks. The problems expose Europe's dependence on US technology, with no homegrown alternatives immediately available.

france24fr.description: Un convoi diplomatique européen a été attaqué samedi par des colons israéliens en Cisjordanie occupée. Bernard Baudoux, maire de la ville d'Aulnoye-Aymeries, a notamment été violemment frappé. Les jours de l'élu de 78 ans ne sont pas en danger, a précisé un diplomate.

france24fr.title: 🔴 ONU : l'ex-président sénégalais Macky Sall retire sa candidature au poste de secrétaire général
Un dialogue est-il encore possible entre le gouvernement et la jeunesse ?
france24fr.description: Prisca Ancion, avocate au barreau de Saint-Denis, Emmanuel Echivard, politologue, sont nos invités.

france24fr.title: ONU : l'ex-président sénégalais Macky Sall retire sa candidature au poste de secrétaire général
france24fr.description: Au lendemain d'un premier vote indicatif sans consensus, l'ancien président sénégalais Macky Sall a annoncé samedi sur les réseaux sociaux qu'il se retirait de la course à la direction de l'ONU. Il assure vouloir vouloir ainsi "favoriser l'émergence d'un candidat de consensus".

france24fr.title: Donald Trump affirme n'avoir pas donné l'ordre de brider Starlink en Ukraine
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a affirmé vendredi qu'il n'avait pas donné l'ordre de brider la déclinaison militaire du réseau Starlink, Starshield, utilisée par les forces ukrainiennes sur le champ de bataille.

france24fr.title: 🔴 17-Octobre en direct : des milliers de manifestants en France, tensions à Paris et Marseille
Mobilisation du 17 octobre : vers une convergence des colères ?
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Echivard, politologue et professeur à Sciences Po Reims, est notre invité.

france24fr.title: Ligue 1 : le Paris Saint-Germain veut confirmer ses progrès à Strasbourg
france24fr.description: Dans la foulée de leur succès de prestige cette semaine sur la pelouse de Manchester City, les Parisiens se déplacent samedi à Strasbourg pour la 7e journée de Ligue 1. Objectif : remporter un quatrième succès de suite en championnat et confirmer la montée en puissance observée en Angleterre, avant de recevoir mardi le redoutable FC Barcelone.

france24fr.title: Mobilisation du 17 octobre : tensions en marge des rassemblements à Paris
france24fr.description: Johan Bodin est en direct de Paris.

france24fr.title: Trump écarte la nouvelle porte-parole de la Maison Blanche, Katie Zacharia
france24fr.description: La porte-parole de la ​Maison Blanche, Katie Zacharia, a été "démise de ses fonctions", a déclaré vendredi un responsable de la Maison Blanche, après ​que le ‌président Donald Trump a déclaré ⁠qu'il lui avait demandé d'envisager de démissionner.

france24fr.title: Le pape Léon XIV quitte l’hôpital et rentre au Vatican quatre jours après son opération
france24fr.description: Quatre jours après l’ablation d’un nodule cancéreux au poumon droit, le pape Léon XIV a quitté samedi l’hôpital Gemelli de Rome pour regagner le Vatican. Souriant, le souverain pontife de 71 ans a salué les fidèles rassemblés devant l’établissement. Jugé "apte à sortir", il doit réciter l’Angélus dimanche depuis la fenêtre de son appartement pontifical.

france24fr.title: Trump exempte la Russie de nouvelles sanctions, en pleine crise avec Kiev
france24fr.description: L'exemption par Donald Trump de sanctions majeures contre la Russie décidées par le Congrès américain, un nouveau camouflet pour l'Ukraine, constitue un moment "historique", s'est félicité samedi le principal négociateur économique de Vladimir Poutine.

france24fr.title: 17 Octobre : des milliers de manifestants attendus dans toute la France
france24fr.description: Des centaines d'actions et rassemblements sont prévus ⁠samedi en ​France dans le cadre d'une mobilisation associant "gilets jaunes", lycéens et étudiants, organisations syndicales et partis de gauche pour dénoncer pêle-mêle la ​hausse du coût de la vie, le manque de moyens de l'Education nationale ou la dégradation des services publics.

france24fr.title: 17 Octobre : journée de mobilisation en France des jeunes et gilets jaunes
france24fr.description: Initialement né sur les réseaux sociaux, l'appel à manifester ce 17 octobre a été relayé par les syndicats ​lycéens qui se ‌mobilisent depuis la mi-septembre pour obtenir de meilleures conditions d'apprentissage.

Berlin: Linke, Grüne und SPD planen Vergesellschaftung von Wohnungen in Berlin
zeit.description: In Berlin haben sich die Parteien darauf geeinigt, im Falle einer Koalition Wohnungen zu vergesellschaften. Die SPD-Spitze sprach von einem »vertretbaren Kompromiss«.

Fußball-Bundesliga: Elversberg jubelt nach Blitzstart gegen FC Augsburg
Loop-One-Festival: Biathlon-Event in München: DSV-Skijäger verpassen Podest
Nach der Wahl: SPD, Grüne und Linke in Berlin prüfen Verpackungssteuer
Bundesliga, 6. Spieltag – Samstag: Dortmund nur Remis gegen Union, Hamburg und Mainz siegen
zeit.description: Dortmund kann gegen Union erneut keinen Sieg erringen, steht aber vorläufig auf Platz eins. Elversberg und Augsburg liefern sich ein torreiches Spiel.

zeit.title: Fußball-Bundesliga: Nächster Rückschlag für BVB - Füllkrug rettet Bremen Punkt
Fußball-Bundesliga: 2:2 nach 0:2 - Werder schafft die nächste Aufholjagd
Tesla Roadster: Der Tesla, der die Fliege macht
zeit.description: Elon Musks fliegender Tesla soll können, was es bislang nur in Sci-Fi-Geschichten gab. Ein paar Sekunden hält sich das Gefährt in der Luft. Ist das mehr als Show?

zeit.title: Krankenkassenreform: Die private Krankenkasse? Abschaffen! Und die gesetzliche? Die auch
zeit.description: Jens Baas, der Chef der Techniker Krankenkasse, fordert einen Neustart bei der Krankenversicherung. Wie der aussehen könnte und was das bringen würde.

zeit.title: Friedrich Merz: Für eine Sache brauchen sie ihn noch
zeit.description: Friedrich Merz vermeidet einen neuen Eklat mit dem Parteinachwuchs. Die Junge Union versucht, den Kanzler nicht weiter zu schädigen – nur einer funkt dazwischen.

zeit.title: Regierungsbildung in Berlin: Grüner Ministerpräsident Özdemir gegen Koalition mit Berliner Linke
zeit.description: Cem Özdemir lehnt eine Zusammenarbeit der Grünen mit der Berliner Linken ab. Er habe nicht grundsätzlich etwas gegen die Partei, in Berlin sei es jedoch ein Sonderfall.

zeit.title: Ergebnis der Berliner Sondierung: Jetzt live: Linke, Grüne und SPD über ihre Sondierung für Berlin
zeit.description: Linke, Grüne und SPD haben die Sondierungen über eine mögliche Regierungsbildung in Berlin abgeschlossen. Verfolgen Sie ihre Pressekonferenz hier live.

nzz.title: Iran-Krieg steht vor neuer Eskalation: Benzinpreise in der Schweiz ziehen an
nzz.description: Die Treibstoffpreise steigen in der Schweiz wegen des Konflikts im Nahen Osten und Trumps «Diesel-Deal» stark. Konsumenten sollten sich langfristig auf hohe Energiepreise einstellen.

nzz.title: Papst Leo verlässt vier Tage nach Krebs-Operation das Krankenhaus
nzz.description: Die Ärzte entliessen Papst Leo nach neuen Untersuchungsergebnissen aus der Klinik. Ob Metastasen vorliegen und welche Behandlung folgt, ist noch unklar.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN POLIZEI - Wegen technischer Störung an Titlis-Bahn müssen 200 Personen evakuiert werden
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Schweiz.

nzz.title: Proteste in Frankreich: Erste Zusammenstösse mit Polizei
nzz.description: Plünderungsversuche, Angriffe auf Ordnungskräfte und Festnahmen begleiten den Protesttag in Frankreich.

nzz.title: Alexander Zverev wird die Nummer eins – und Boris Becker ist wieder sein grösster Fan
nzz.description: Die deutsche Tennislegende begleitet Zverev seit je sehr eng. Er ist Förderer und scharfer Kritiker zugleich. Mit den jüngsten Erfolgen des 29-Jährigen wandelt sich ihr ambivalentes Verhältnis einmal mehr.

nzz.title: Coreweave, ein Entwickler von Rechenzentren, steckt in Schwierigkeiten – Kritiker sehen darin ein Frühwarnzeichen für die ganze KI-Industrie
nzz.description: Die Zinsen steigen, und der Widerstand gegen Datenzentren nimmt zu. An den Finanzmärkten wachsen deshalb die Zweifel, ob das eng mit dem Chipentwickler Nvidia verbandelte Unternehmen überlebensfähig ist.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Das Bashing der Superreichen führt in die Irre: Europa hat nicht zu viele, sondern zu wenige Milliardäre – und erst noch die falschen
nzz.description: Selfmade-Milliardäre wie Elon Musk oder Jeff Bezos verdienen Anerkennung. Weniger gut stehen Europas Superreiche da: Hier haben die meisten ihr Vermögen geerbt.

nzz.title: Der Nato-Siegesplan, der eine Niederlage überspielt
nzz.description: Die Nato stellte am Sicherheitsforum in Warschau das Konzept vor, wie sie einen russischen Angriff abwehren will: ein Operationsplan nach Lehrbuch, allerdings ohne offensive Elemente zur aktiven Verteidigung.

nzz.title: Teurere Festhypotheken: Für Immobilienkäufer geht die Zeit des billigen Geldes zu Ende
nzz.description: Der Leitzins in der Schweiz bleibt bei 0 Prozent, dennoch verteuern sich die eigenen vier Wände. Der Preissprung trifft viele Hausbesitzer unvorbereitet, oft just im Moment einer Anschlussfinanzierung.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Merz und Macron denken bei Autos planwirtschaftlich – zum Schaden der Steuerzahler und der Schweiz
nzz.description: Die beiden Politiker möchten europäische E-Autos mit Kaufprämien fördern. Gleichzeitig nehmen sie Retuschen am Verbrenner-Aus vor. Es ist eine sehr unheilige Allianz.

nzz.title: Nach der Eiszeit unter Orban nähern sich Ungarn und die Ukraine vorsichtig an
nzz.description: Seit dem Machtwechsel hat Budapest einen klaren Kurswechsel gegenüber Russland vollzogen. Das macht den neuen Regierungschef Magyar aber noch nicht zu einem glühenden Unterstützer der Ukraine. Nun gelang jedoch ein Durchbruch.

nzz.title: Die Schaltsekunde verschwindet, die Schaltstunde kommt – aber erst in einigen tausend Jahren
nzz.description: Die koordinierte Weltzeit UTC ist der Taktgeber der modernen Zivilisation. Jetzt verliert sie ihr grösstes Manko: ihre Sprunghaftigkeit.

nzz.title: El Salvadors Präsident Bukele erwägt die Freilassung Tausender Drogenkrimineller. Ist es das Ende seiner «mano dura»?
nzz.description: Bisher ging Nayib Bukele gnadenlos gegen Gangs vor. Umso überraschender sind nun die versöhnlichen Töne. Derweil hat auch Costa Rica ein Mega-Gefängnis nach Bukeles Vorbild gebaut.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - Geheimdienstexperte zur Spionage durch China und Russland: «Wenn ich ausländischen Kollegen erzähle, wie klein der NDB ist, können sie es kaum glauben»
nzz.description: Chinesische und russische Spionage nehme in der Schweiz spürbar zu, sagt Adrian Hänni, Historiker und Experte für Nachrichtendienste. Der Fall Hanning zeige, dass auch private Dienste immer aktiver würden.

nzz.title: Krokodile im Gefängnisgraben, Rekorde im Siedlungsbau: Wie Israels extreme Rechte um Stimmen kämpft
nzz.description: Israel steht kurz vor der Parlamentswahl. Wer gewinnt? Seit dem Massaker vom 7. Oktober ist Israel weiter nach rechts gerückt, aber Benjamin Netanyahus Partei profitiert davon kaum. Die Stimmen holen sich andere.

nzz.title: Warum dieses rechnende Pferd hundert Jahre nach seinem Tod in der künstlichen Intelligenz Karriere macht
nzz.description: Der kluge Hans wurde 1904 in Berlin zu einer Weltsensation. Er konnte scheinbar rechnen, lesen und sich sprachlich mitteilen. Später fand man heraus, dass er eine ganz andere Fähigkeit besass. Das macht ihn heute zum Sinnbild für das grösste Problem der KI.

spiegel.title: Oberstdorf: Feuerwehrmann stirbt bei Lauf an Skiflugschanze im Oberallgäu
spiegel.description: Mehr als 1000 Stufen mit voller Ausrüstung: Bei einem Feuerwehrlauf an der Skiflugschanze im bayerischen Oberstdorf ist ein Mann ums Leben gekommen. Die genaue Todesursache ist noch unklar.

spiegel.title: Fußball-Bundesliga: Füllkrug-Tore, Werder-Wende und der HSV gewinnt wieder
spiegel.description: Werder Bremen benötigt ein 0:2, um aufzudrehen. Der HSV gewinnt dank eines unwahrscheinlichen Torjägers erneut. Elversberg zündet ein Feuerwerk, der BVB dagegen keins. Das war der Bundesliga-Nachmittag am Samstag.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Wolodymyr Selenskyj beklagt anhaltende Drosselung von Starlink in der Ukraine
spiegel.description: Nach Angaben des ukrainischen Präsidenten kann Kyjiws Militär wegen der Störung von Starlink wichtige Drohnen weiterhin nicht steuern. In anderen europäischen Länder funktioniere der Dienst.

spiegel.title: Modelabel Kitschy Couture: »Pforzheim. Die geilste Stadt der Welt«
spiegel.description: Sie entwerfen Outfits für Nina Chuba und statten US-Stars aus: Die Designerinnen Abarna Kugathasan und Claudia Walter machen gerade mit ihrem jungen Modelabel Karriere. Aber sie wollen mehr.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump beim Wahlkampf in Georgia für die Midterms: »Ich unterstütze meinen Präsidenten trotzdem«
spiegel.description: Donald Trump tritt im Swing-State Georgia vor seinen Anhängern auf. Hohe Inflation, der Krieg mit Iran – es scheint egal zu sein, was der US-Präsident tut. Für sie ist er unfehlbar.

spiegel.title: FC Chelsea: Torwart Martínez nach Kopfzusammenstoß im Krankenhaus
spiegel.description: Ein Luftzweikampf endete für Chelseas Torwart Emiliano Martínez womöglich mit einer schweren Kopfverletzung. Das Spiel musste für rund zehn Minuten unterbrochen werden.

spiegel.title: Papst Leo XIV. ist nach Lungenkrebs-Operation in den Vatikan zurückgekehrt
spiegel.description: Erst am Dienstag war dem Papst ein Teil seines rechten Lungenflügels entfernt worden. Früher als erwartet verließ Leo XIV. am Samstag das Krankenhaus und wurde in den Vatikan gebracht.

spiegel.title: »Grand Condé«: Französisches Museum zeigt berühmten rosa Diamanten
spiegel.description: In Frankreich wird ein berühmter Diamant nach langer Zeit wieder ausgestellt: Der »Grand Condé« war 1926 gestohlen worden – und wurde damals angeblich auf spektakuläre Weise gefunden.

spiegel.title: Selbsttest zu Alter und Weisheit: Werden Sie weiser – oder nur älter?
spiegel.description: Je länger Sie leben, desto mehr Zipperlein kommen hinzu. Mit unserem Check erkennen Sie, ob Sie sich mit dem Älterwerden gut arrangieren. Und was noch fehlt, um zufrieden zu sein.

spiegel.title: Immobilien: Wie Emanuel Heisenberg die Sanierung von Wohnhäusern revolutionieren will
spiegel.description: Emanuel Heisenberg, Enkel des berühmten Physikers, will den Wohnungsmarkt revolutionieren. Er verspricht radikal weniger Energieverbrauch – und doppelt so schnelle Bauarbeiten.

spiegel.title: Parteienwerbung: Wenn Kampagnen von Campact & Co. Wahlen mitentscheiden
spiegel.description: Die Organisation Campact und andere Akteure unterstützten ausgewählte Parteien mit mehreren 100.000 Euro in Landtagswahlkämpfen. Solche Kampagnen scheinen immer attraktiver zu werden – und sind umstritten.

spiegel.title: Bangladesch: Feuer in Hotelanlage in Cox's Bazar, mindestens zehn Tote
spiegel.description: Bei einem Feuer in einem Strandresort in Bangladesch sind zehn Touristen ums Leben gekommen. Eine Behörde spricht von »mangelhaften« Brandschutzvorkehrungen – und dass die Anlage ohne Genehmigung errichtet worden sei.

spiegel.title: Cyberangriff auf Hochschulen – Noten und Stundenpläne offline
spiegel.description: Ein Cyberangriff auf Hochschulen in Baden-Württemberg hat weitreichende Folgen: Viele wichtige Systeme sind offline, auch Lehrkräfte bekommen ihr Geld nicht überwiesen. Wer hinter dem Angriff steckt, ist noch unklar.

spiegel.title: Tunesien: Kais Saied in der Kritik, Tausende protestieren gegen den Autokraten
spiegel.description: Tunesiens Opposition hat gegen Machthaber Kais Saied protestiert. Die Tunesier fordern die Freilassung politischer Gefangener und machen das Regime für die Wirtschaftskrise verantwortlich.

spiegel.title: Saudi-Arabien: Droht nach den Angriffen der Huthis ein offener Krieg mit Iran?
spiegel.description: Pilger werden Opfer eines Raketenangriffs: Für Saudi-Arabien waren die jüngsten Angriffe der Huthis ein Schock. Wie wird Kronprinz Mohammed bin Salman reagieren? Nahost-Korrespondentin Dunja Ramadan über die brandgefährliche Situation.

spiegel.title: Ukrainekrieg: So sieht der Alltag im Frontgebiet in Isjum aus
spiegel.description: Witalij Papirnyj und Lilija Dschemiljewa mussten wegen der Russen ihr Zuhause verlassen. Nun wollen sie in der Stadt Isjum neu anfangen. Doch die Front rückt immer näher.

spiegel.title: Männlichkeit in Uni- und Collegefilmen: Was Campusfilme mit dem Fall »Cornell Seven« verbindet
spiegel.description: Die bewusstlose, alkoholisierte Frau. Der Mann, der ihre Wehrlosigkeit als günstige Gelegenheit begreift. Dieses Motiv gehörte lange zur Collegekomödie. Was haben die Filme mit dem Fall an der Cornell University zu tun?

spiegel.title: Dorothee Elmigers »Die Holländerinnen«: Bühnenadaption im Deutschen Theater Berlin
spiegel.description: Der hochgelobte und rätselhafte Roman »Die Holländerinnen« ist ein beliebter Stoff auf vielen deutschen Theaterbühnen – in Berlin macht Regisseur Jan Friedrich eine großartige Bühnen-Geisterstunde daraus.

observador.title: "Chapo é o Presidente de Moçambique com o maior número de...
observador.description: Arrisca-se a ir 20 anos para a prisão, mas diz-se tranquilo. Acusa o líder moçambicano de ter o maior registo de assassinatos de opositores políticos. E explica porque gosta de Flávio Bolsonaro.

observador.title: Gio Rodrigues vai transformar desfile em protesto
observador.description: Passarela no Palácio de Queluz vai ser tornada num palco de protesto contra a violência e em defesa dos direitos dos portugueses.

observador.title: Atlético de Madrid vence com golo tardio de Alex Baena
observador.description: Clube reduziu o atraso para o Barcelona para apenas dois pontos e isolou-se no segundo lugar da La Liga.

observador.title: Frelimo anuncia apoio à candidatura de Daniel Chapo em 2029
observador.description: Partido anunciou que vai apoiar a candidatura presidencial de Daniel Chapo nas próximas eleições, previstas para 2029. Frelimo diz que Chapo estabilizou o país, depois dos protestos violentos de 2024.

observador.title: As notícias das 16h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: IL não viraria costas a Passos, mas não aceitaria Chega
observador.description: Iniciativa Liberal considera que Passos Coelho está focado no certo: reformas para o país. Porém, liberais não entendem ideia de falar em coligação com o Chega e alertam para "erro crasso".

observador.title: Bis de Pedro Neto garante triunfo do Chelsea
observador.description: Avançado português garantiu o 2-0 do Chelsea na visita ao Everton. Clube está provisoriamente no quarto lugar da Premier League.

observador.title: Mais de três mil pessoas em protestos na Tunísia
observador.description: Contra o aumento do custo de vida, mais de três mil pessoas participaram em protesto na capital Tunes.

observador.title: Ceuta acolhe mais de três mil menores
observador.description: Governo de Ceuta anunciou que acolhe atualmente 3.086 menores, em comparação com as 180 crianças no início de julho. Centros estão sobrelotados, com 106 vezes mais ocupação do que o suposto.

observador.title: 15h. Lisboa. Manifestação contra o custo de vida já arrancou
observador.description: As manifestações no Porto e em Coimbra terminaram, com nova concentração marcada para 24 de novembro, dia da votação do OE. Ainda, no desporto, Iúri Leitão é campeão do mundo de omnium.

observador.title: Como mais 2 linhas e Gare do Oriente renovada mudam Lisboa
observador.description: Projeto de 700 milhões de euros vai quadruplicar linha ferroviária de Roma-Areeiro até à Linha do Norte. Prevê novos viadutos ferroviários na zona oriental e uma Gare do Oriente renovada e maior.

observador.title: Eis ”O Homem Que Mordeu o Cão" com que Markl sempre sonhou
observador.description: Estreia-se na realização menos de um ano depois de dois AVCs e as histórias absurdas, mas reais, que conta na rádio chegam ao cinema. Fomos saber como tudo isto ganha corpo de longa-metragem.

observador.title: Mais um dia para esquecer: Miguel desiste a meio da corrida
observador.description: Miguel Oliveira não conseguiu confirmar registos top 10 dos treinos livres na qualificação, saiu da 13.ª posição, ganhou um lugar mas acabou por desistir a 11 voltas do final com problemas na moto.

observador.title: 14h. França. Mais de uma centena de detidos em protestos
observador.description: O dia está a ser marcado por novos protestos, com confrontos entre manifestantes e a polícia. Ainda, Comissão Europeia diz que as sanções contra Moscovo estão a resultar, mas é preciso fazer mais.

observador.title: Ex-Presidente do Senegal retira-se de corrida da ONU
observador.description: Macky Sall anunciou que retira a sua candidatura ao cargo de secretário-geral da ONU. Nenhum candidato obteve consenso na primeira votação.

observador.title: Fokina surpreende Zverev e apura-se para a final do Masters
observador.description: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina derrotou nas meias-finais o alemão Alexander Zverev, primeiro cabeça de série do torneio chinês, e qualificou-se para a final do Masters 1.000 de Xangai.

observador.title: Benjamin Moser e os judeus que se opuseram ao sionismo
observador.description: Como é que a memória judaica se constrói através daqueles que criticaram a criação de um estado soberano? O Observador faz a pré-publicação de um excerto do livro "Antissionismo", a publicar dia 19.

observador.title: Do tratado ao arranque canhão: Iúri sagra-se campeão mundial
observador.description: Potenciou pontos fortes, controlou eventuais fragilidades, teve mais um dia de exceção: ganhou o scratch, foi terceiro no tempo e na eliminação e voou na parte final dos pontos para vencer a prova.

letemps.description:

phys-org.title: Hand-cranked device tells blood type and red cell levels in 1 minute
phys-org.description: When someone is badly injured, doctors urgently need two facts: the patient's blood type, so that a transfusion is safe, and their hematocrit, the share of the blood made up of red blood cells, which reveals blood loss or anemia. Hospitals measure both with large machines that need electricity and trained staff, which are often unavailable in ambulances, disaster zones or remote clinics.

phys-org.title: Salt crystals could hold clues to life beneath Enceladus's ice
phys-org.description: The ocean beneath Saturn's moon Enceladus lies under kilometers of ice, but some of its contents do reach the surface. Jets near the south pole spray out water vapor and icy particles, offering a way to investigate the hidden ocean without drilling down to it.

phys-org.title: Australian scavengers don't just eat everything and slink away. They approach a carcass like a buffet
phys-org.description: When scientists talk about scavengers, you might imagine an animal sniffing out or stumbling across a carcass, eating as much as possible and slinking away.

phys-org.title: The ambiguous costs of climate change
phys-org.description: As human activity has increased temperatures globally, determining the costs directly incurred by climate change is challenging. The effects of climate change on extreme weather events—such as hurricanes and heat waves—can be locally specific and variable, and observations and climate modeling might not accurately capture those effects.

phys-org.title: Lone, starless cloud may be a 'dark' galaxy
phys-org.description: Astronomers using China's FAST radio telescope have discovered a compact cloud of hydrogen with no visible stars or galaxy around it. This could be one of the strongest candidates yet for an isolated "dark galaxy," containing nearly 500,000 times the sun's mass in neutral hydrogen. The discovery paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 24.

phys-org.title: Red-sensitive pigments in mantis shrimp eyes act as reversible light switches
phys-org.description: With about 30 visual pigments, compared to just three in humans, mantis shrimp possess a visual system that remains a mystery. Researchers from ULiège and Humboldt University in Berlin have, for the first time, analyzed these pigments one by one and discovered that some detect red light that very few animals can perceive. This finding, published in Science Advances, has potential applications in optogenetics.

phys-org.title: Electrical sliding switches graphene between magnetic states
phys-org.description: In a discovery that could offer a new way to control quantum properties in two-dimensional materials, researchers at Cornell have found that electrically sliding the layers of ultrathin graphene can switch the material between distinct magnetic states that persist even after the voltage is removed.

phys-org.title: Global survey links financial hardship to lower trust in science
phys-org.description: Poor access to health care, limited local influence over research priorities and an unequal distribution of scientific benefits are undermining public confidence in science, experts warn, following the release of a global trust survey.

phys-org.title: Popular song lyrics express less emotion over time, analysis of 38K+ songs finds
phys-org.description: New research from Michigan State University finds that popular music has gradually become less explicit about emotion and relationships—both across generations of artists and within artists' careers.

phys-org.title: During El Niño, a perfect storm of weather systems could spell disaster for the Great Barrier Reef
phys-org.description: The strong El Niño currently under way in the Pacific Ocean raises the specter of marine heat waves and coral bleaching once again threatening Australia's iconic Great Barrier Reef. And now new research has revealed the complex interplay of atmospheric patterns and weather systems thousands of kilometers apart that can combine in a recipe potentially fatal for coral reefs.

phys-org.title: Optical imaging links altered metabolism and oxygen use in Alzheimer's disease
phys-org.description: Alzheimer's disease is best known for its effects on memory and cognition, but the disease also involves changes in how brain cells produce and use energy. Mitochondria, the structures that supply much of a cell's energy, can become dysfunctional in Alzheimer's disease. At the same time, changes in blood flow and oxygen availability may place additional demands on brain tissue. phys-org.title: How animal identifiability affects children's food choices
phys-org.description: Naming a chicken and describing its favorite habits is enough to make preschoolers choose poultry less often. This effect translates into verbal declarations and actual meal choices, but food preferences still most often win over empathy, according to a new paper by researchers from SWPS University.

phys-org.description: What happens when political violence is presented as a justified response to threat or injustice coming from an out-group? A study by Ursula Daxecker, director at the Max Planck Institute for Politics and Social Science in Göttingen, and Neeraj Prasad of the University of Amsterdam, published in The Journal of Politics, finds that legitimizing violence can increase public approval of both violence and the parties involved in it. phys-org.title: Scientists uncover mystery of how snail shells coil to the right or to the left
phys-org.description: Scientists have discovered a gene that determines whether Japanese snails develop shells that are left- or right-coiling—with implications for understanding the underlying handedness of our own bodies. The researchers from the University of Nottingham and Tohoku University studied wild Euhadra snails in Japan to understand what makes one snail a mirror image of another.

phys-org.title: Rabbits were a medieval royal luxury in England—until the Black Death made them commonplace
phys-org.description: The European rabbit is a common sight in the British countryside today. Yet it was not always so. They are not native to the British Isles and are one of the most devastating invasive species.

phys-org.title: Astronomer leads global team on NASA mission to create unprecedented view of the early universe
phys-org.description: A University of Missouri astronomer is leading a team of 130 researchers from 62 institutions—including NASA, the California Institute of Technology, Princeton University and Harvard University—on an ambitious mission to capture an unprecedented view of the early universe.

phys-org.title: Plants shift gene activity within minutes of entering spaceflight, experiment reveals
phys-org.description: Plants begin responding to spaceflight almost immediately after leaving Earth, according to a new University of Florida study that captured the earliest stages of biological adaptation during a commercial suborbital mission. Published in the journal npj Microgravity, the study reports the results of an experiment conducted by a UF astronaut during Blue Origin's New Shepard NS-26 flight on Aug. 29, 2024.

phys-org.title: New 3D model reveals how shadows reshape chemistry in stellar nurseries
phys-org.description: How do young stars reshape the clouds from which they are born? A new high-resolution 3D model developed by an international team led by Dr Brandt Gaches from the University of Duisburg-Essen shows how the uneven structure of stellar nurseries creates shadows that alter their chemistry and influence the infrared emission observed by the James Webb Space Telescope. The model has now been published in Astronomy & Astrophysics.

undark.title: Podcast: Is There a Population Crisis?

Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

proj-syn.title: A Global Euro Must First Win Over Europe
proj-syn.description: In a world of competing currency blocs, the euro is the dollar’s most credible rival. But for it to become a genuine counterweight to the greenback, the European Union must strengthen its financial foundations and expand its reach, starting with the member states that have not adopted it despite being obliged to do so.

proj-syn.title: Japan Needs Higher Interest Rates
proj-syn.description: In 2012, when Japan was dealing with chronic deflation, policymakers were right to embrace monetary easing, including lower interest rates. Today, however, Japan faces the opposite problem: a weak yen, combined with higher interest rates in the US, calls for a much tighter monetary policy.

proj-syn.title: A Middle-Powers Grand Strategy to Prevent Atrocities
proj-syn.description: Many governments have leverage to prevent atrocity crimes, yet lack the machinery to turn warnings into consistent, accountable action before it is too late. Now that three of the five permanent members of the Security Council are undercutting the postwar legal order, middle powers most close the gap.

proj-syn.title: Unleashing Africa’s Women Agripreneurs
proj-syn.description: Across Sub-Saharan Africa, women workers dominate agriculture but rarely capture the sector’s economic value. With a systematic approach to closing the gap, policymakers, NGOs, and philanthropic organizations could unlock a $1 trillion market and transform the continent’s food systems for the better.

proj-syn.title: Low Expectations for Israel’s Election
proj-syn.description: Benjamin Netanyahu has led Israel into a trap in which ever-increasing strategic commitments are outstripping the productive base that finances them, and the goodwill on which its alliances depend is being destroyed. While a new government would not transform Israeli foreign policy, it could begin to drag Israel out of its morass.

proj-syn.title: From AI Boom to Economic Bust
proj-syn.description: Contrary to tech optimists' rosy predictions, AI may prove to be a drag on growth. By concentrating wealth and economic opportunities in a few cities while destroying the low-cost jobs that have historically fueled global development, the technology could end up making much of the world poorer and more divided.

proj-syn.title: The Institutional Roots of Policy Nonsense
proj-syn.description: At a time when antimicrobial resistance threatens public health and our long-term economic well-being, tax policies favor financial engineering at the expense of developing new antibiotics. Similarly perverse incentives are at the heart of out-of-control public spending.

proj-syn.title: Is Christian Democracy Finished?
proj-syn.description: Traditionally, Christian Democrats believed that taking care of all groups in society could create a harmonious balance that would prevent instability and self-destructive infighting. But the conditions that enabled this strategy have changed, particularly in Germany, where Christian Democrats must reconnect with a different part of their history.

proj-syn.title: Independent AI Auditing Now
proj-syn.description: Recent hacking incidents confirm the need for independent scrutiny not only of what AI systems are capable of, but also of what their developers are doing to minimize harm and communicate honestly with the public. Even if AI auditing is still at an early stage, other industries have already provided a playbook.

proj-syn.title: Strict Liability for AI Executives
proj-syn.description: As an OpenAI whistleblower recently explained, AI executives have knowingly fostered a culture that “guarantees periodic failures,” the scale of which is “growing as systems get more capable.” This approach hinges on an expectation of impunity, which is why AI firms must be held legally accountable for the harm their agents cause.

proj-syn.title: Who Will Pay to Preserve Tropical Forests?
proj-syn.description: For decades, the international community has acknowledged the extraordinary value of tropical forests while failing to invest adequately in their conservation. The Tropical Forest Forever Facility, launched at last year’s United Nations Climate Change Conference, could help close this financing gap.

proj-syn.title: Why Following in Milei’s Footsteps Would Be Bad for Brazil
proj-syn.description: Far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro holds up Argentine President Javier Milei’s economic program as a model for Brazil. But Milei's economic experiment has been a failure, leaving millions of Argentinians worse off and effectively turning their heavily indebted country into a client of the United States.

proj-syn.title: How Worried Should We Be About the Global Economy?
proj-syn.description: The risks to the global economy—including high inflation, soaring public debt, market concentration, and geopolitical volatility—are well known. But it is worth underscoring just how rare and dangerous it is for all of them to be salient at the same time.

proj-syn.title: How a Pause on Frontier AI Could Work
proj-syn.description: Whether the development of frontier AI should be paused is for policymakers to decide. But they should recognize that highly concentrated hardware supply chains make a pause feasible and, if implemented properly, likely to be sustainable.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Latest Gift to Putin
proj-syn.description: Unable to win his foolish war against Iran, Donald Trump blames its consequences on Ukraine and uses the lie to justify ending sanctions against Russia, thereby extending that war as well. His diesel deal with the Kremlin is less about lowering gas prices for Americans and more about submitting to Vladimir Putin.

proj-syn.title: China’s Panda Diplomacy Is Losing Its Charm
proj-syn.description: Since giving a pair of giant pandas to the Smithsonian’s National Zoo in 1972 following President Richard Nixon’s visit to Beijing, China has used panda loans as a means of projecting a harmless and friendly image globally. But it was always an act—and foreign audiences are no longer falling for it.

proj-syn.title: The Blindness of China’s All-Seeing State
proj-syn.description: China's relentless surveillance has taught people to perform obedience and loyalty, while keeping their beliefs hidden. This creates a dilemma for the ruling Communist Party: repression distorts the very information the government needs to understand society.

proj-syn.title: A Stronger Renminbi Is No Quick Fix for Global Imbalances
proj-syn.description: The near-consensus among financial commentators is that China's currency is undervalued, driving global imbalances. But the renminbi's weakness reflects weak domestic demand, and pursuing currency appreciation without addressing that issue head-on would be counterproductive for everyone.
